breakfast.name: Qurutob (Bread in Yogurt)
instructions: Tear bread into bowl
Pour yogurt sauce over
Top with onion, tomatoes, herbs, oil
breakfast.description: Tajikistan's national dish — bread soaked in yogurt sauce.

breakfast.name: Non (Tajik Bread)
instructions: Make dough, rise
Shape round, stamp center
Top with seeds
Bake in tandoor oven
breakfast.description: Round stamped bread baked in a tandoor.

breakfast.name: Shirchoy (Salted Milk Tea)
instructions: Shirchoy is the Central Asian salted milk tea -- Tajikistan and neighboring regions
Tea brewed strong and mixed with hot milk
Salted, not sweetened -- the savory tea tradition of nomadic Central Asia
A small piece of butter sometimes added
The salt: the nomadic herder tradition -- salt was valuable and flavoring
Drunk with bread in the morning
breakfast.description: Tajik salted milk tea -- shirchoy, strong black tea mixed with hot milk and salt (no sugar: the Central Asian nomadic tradition of salted, not sweet, tea). Drunk in the morning with bread. The salt tradition comes from nomadic herder culture where salt was a flavor and preservation essential.

breakfast.name: Fatir (Flaky Baked Flatbread)
ingredients: Lamb fat (rendered -- rubbed between layers for the flaky texture)
instructions: Fatir is the Tajik and Uzbek layered baked flatbread
A flaky, rich flatbread made by layering the dough with fat
Baked in a tandoor (clay oven) -- or on a flat griddle
Denser and richer than non (Tajik round flatbread)
Eaten with tea as a breakfast staple
breakfast.description: Tajik layered baked flatbread -- fatir, dough layered with rendered lamb fat between layers (creating flakiness), baked in a tandoor. Richer and denser than regular non flatbread. Eaten with tea for breakfast.

lunch.name: Oshi Palav (Tajik Plov)
instructions: Fry onion and meat
Add carrots, chickpeas, cumin
Add rice and water
Cook covered until done
Garnish with barberries
lunch.description: Fragrant lamb pilaf — the crown of Tajik cooking.

lunch.name: Mastoba (Rice and Meat Soup)
instructions: Brown lamb with onion
Add water, carrots, tomatoes
Add rice, simmer until done
Serve with yogurt
lunch.description: Rice soup with lamb and yogurt.

lunch.name: Lagman (Hand-Pulled Noodle Soup)
ingredients: Wheat flour dough (stretched into long hand-pulled noodles)
instructions: Lagman is the Central Asian hand-pulled noodle soup -- from Uyghur origin
The Uyghur (Xinjiang) noodle tradition spread across the Silk Road
The noodles are hand-pulled -- stretched repeatedly until long and thin
Served in a tomato-vegetable and lamb broth
The noodles are the craft -- making them is a skill
Eaten across Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan
lunch.description: Tajik hand-pulled noodle soup -- lagman, wheat dough stretched into long hand-pulled noodles, served in a lamb-tomato-vegetable broth. Uyghur (Xinjiang) origin spread via the Silk Road. Eaten across Central Asia. The hand-pulling of the noodles is the craft.

lunch.name: Kurutob (Bread in Yoghurt Sauce)
ingredients: Fatir or non (flatbread -- torn into pieces)
Qurut (dried sour yoghurt balls -- dissolved in water to make a sauce)
instructions: Kurutob is the Tajik national dish -- bread soaked in a qurut sauce
Qurut: dried balls of sour yoghurt (drained, salted, and dried in the sun) -- reconstituted with water
The torn bread absorbs the tangy, sour qurut sauce
Raw sliced onion, herbs, and chilli on top
Butter or oil drizzled over
Eaten communally from a large flat dish
The qurut preservation: yoghurt dried into shelf-stable balls -- Silk Road travel food
lunch.description: Tajik bread in sour yoghurt sauce -- fatir flatbread torn and soaked in qurut sauce (dried yoghurt balls dissolved: qurut was dried for shelf-stable Silk Road travel), topped with raw onion, herbs, and chilli. The Tajik national dish, eaten communally.

lunch.name: Samsa (Baked Meat Pastry)
ingredients: Flaky pastry dough (layered with fat -- or bought)
Onion (lots -- equal to the meat volume)
instructions: Samsa are the Central Asian baked meat pastries -- related to the South Asian samosa
The shared root: the Persian word sanbosag
In Central Asia, samsa are baked (not fried) and made with flaky dough
The filling: minced lamb with a large amount of onion
The onion: equal volume to the meat -- it sweats and becomes soft and sweet
Baked in a tandoor for the authentic version
Sesame seeds on top
lunch.description: Tajik baked meat pastry -- flaky dough filled with minced lamb and equal volumes of onion (the onion sweats soft and sweet during baking), sealed, sesame seeds on top, baked in a tandoor. Related to South Asian samosa via Persian sanbosag. Baked, not fried.

dinner.name: Sambusa Tajik (Baked Pastries)
instructions: Make dough, cut squares
Fill with spiced lamb
Fold triangles, seal
Bake in tandoor or oven at 200°C 25 min

dinner.name: Lagman (Pulled Noodle Soup)
instructions: Stretch noodles by hand
Stir-fry lamb and vegetables
Add broth
Cook noodles, add to soup

dinner.name: Shurbo (Lamb and Vegetable Soup)
instructions: Shurbo is the Tajik lamb and vegetable soup -- the everyday family meal
Lamb pieces simmered for a long time until the broth is rich
Vegetables added whole or in large pieces
Simple and nourishing
A soup that is also a main course
dinner.description: Tajik lamb and vegetable soup -- bone-in lamb simmered until the broth is rich, with potatoes, carrots, and turnips. Simple, nourishing, the everyday family meal. Also serves as the main course.

dinner.name: Kabob (Grilled Skewers)
instructions: Central Asian kabob is ground lamb pressed onto metal skewers
Seasoned simply with onion, cumin, and coriander
Grilled over charcoal
Served with flatbread and raw onion salad (onion with sumac or vinegar)
The fat in the lamb drips into the fire -- the char is the flavor
dinner.description: Tajik grilled lamb skewers -- ground fatty lamb mixed with grated onion and cumin, pressed onto metal skewers and chargrilled. Served with flatbread and raw onion salad. The fat dripping into the charcoal creates the char that flavors the kabob.

dinner.name: Mantu (Steamed Dumplings)
ingredients: Sour cream or qurut sauce (to serve)
instructions: Mantu are the Tajik large steamed dumplings
Closely related to Turkish manti and Mongolian buuz -- the Silk Road dumpling family
Larger than Chinese dumplings -- more substantial
Filled with seasoned lamb and onion
Steamed in layers in a tiered pot
Served with sour cream or qurut sauce and butter
dinner.description: Tajik large steamed dumplings -- mantu, thin dough filled with ground lamb and onion, steamed in a tiered pot. Closely related to Turkish manti and Mongolian buuz (the Silk Road dumpling family). Served with sour cream and butter. Larger than Chinese dumplings.

snacks.name: Fatir (Layered Bread)
instructions: Make dough, spread butter, fold layers
Roll thin
Cook on griddle

imageCredit.author: Prepared by Obayd based on PD text from the Mushaf al-Madina software

snacks.name: Non (Round Flatbread)
instructions: Non is the Tajik and Uzbek round flatbread -- the bread of Central Asia
Baked in a tandoor: stuck to the hot inner wall of the clay oven
The center is pressed with a nona (bread stamp) to create a pattern and prevent bubbling
Sesame seeds in the center
The bread is a cultural artifact: passed respectfully, never placed face-down
Breaking bread (non) with someone is a hospitality ritual
snacks.description: Tajik round tandoor flatbread -- non, dough stamped with a pattern in the center (to prevent bubbling) and sesame seeds, baked by sticking to the hot inner wall of the tandoor. Breaking non is a hospitality ritual. The bread must never be placed face-down.

snacks.name: Qurut (Dried Yoghurt Balls)
instructions: Qurut are the Central Asian dried yoghurt balls -- the Silk Road snack
Yoghurt strained, salted, and formed into balls
Sun-dried until hard and shelf-stable
Intensely sour and salty
Eaten as a snack or dissolved in water for a sauce
Used in kurutob (the national dish)
The preservation: before refrigeration, qurut kept dairy protein available during travel
snacks.description: Tajik dried yoghurt balls -- strained yoghurt salted and formed into balls, sun-dried until hard and shelf-stable. Intensely sour and salty. Eaten as a snack or dissolved in water for kurutob sauce. The Silk Road preservation technique: dairy protein dried for travel.

snacks.name: Halvaitar (Flour Halva)
instructions: Halvaitar is the Tajik flour halva -- made by toasting flour in butter
The flour is fried in hot butter until golden and nutty
Water and sugar added to form a thick paste
A simple, satisfying sweet made from pantry staples
Eaten at celebrations and as a comfort sweet
snacks.description: Tajik flour halva -- flour toasted in butter until golden and nutty, water and sugar added to form a thick sweet paste. Made from pantry staples. Eaten at celebrations and as a simple comfort food.

desserts.name: Halvaitar (Flour Halva)
instructions: Toast flour in butter until golden
Make sugar syrup
Combine, stir until thick
Pour into mold

desserts.name: Kishti (Walnut Sweet)
instructions: Kishti are the Tajik walnut sweets
Walnuts preserved in honey or sugar syrup
Simple and satisfying -- the walnut and honey are the flavor
Tajikistan grows excellent walnuts
desserts.description: Tajik walnut sweets -- halved walnuts preserved in honey or sugar syrup. Tajikistan grows excellent walnuts; the honey-walnut combination is simple and satisfying.

desserts.name: Shir Birinj (Rice Pudding)
instructions: Shir birinj is the Persian-origin rice pudding eaten across Central Asia and Iran
Shir = milk, birinj = rice in Persian/Tajik
Rice cooked in milk with cardamom and rosewater
The Persian culinary influence on Tajik food -- Tajik and Persian (Dari/Farsi) are closely related languages
desserts.description: Tajik Persian-heritage rice pudding -- shir birinj (milk + rice in Persian/Tajik), short-grain rice cooked in milk with cardamom and rosewater. The Persian culinary influence on Tajik food reflects the linguistic connection: Tajik and Farsi are closely related.

drinks.name: Shirchoy (Milk Tea)
instructions: Brew green tea
Add milk, salt, and butter
Serve hot
drinks.description: Salty milk tea with butter — Central Asian tradition.

drinks.name: Compot (Fruit Drink)
instructions: Simmer dried fruits with sugar
Cool, serve cold with fruit

drinks.name: Dugh (Sour Yoghurt Drink)
instructions: Dugh is the Tajik and Persian sour yoghurt drink
Very similar to Turkish ayran and Indian lassi (salted version)
Yoghurt thinned with cold water, salted, and flavored with dried mint
Refreshing in the Central Asian heat
The mint is the Tajik flavor preference over the Turkish salted-only ayran
drinks.description: Tajik sour yoghurt drink -- dugh, yoghurt thinned with cold water, salted, and flavored with dried mint. Related to Turkish ayran and Indian lassi. Refreshing in the Central Asian heat. The mint distinguishes it from the Turkish salted-only version.
